title: Architecture: replace agent-held BRC waits with deterministic event-pump + durable per-agent memory
summary: Reframe a consensus agent from a persistent participant that holds a wait_loop into a stateless per-event handler the wrapper invokes. The deterministic outer loop is the wrapper (`bash -c` heredoc in orchestrator/consensus_wrapper.py:116-713), blocking on `egg-orch message wait-loop`; on each actionable event it invokes `claude -p` (SDK-native one-shot, no custom harness) with the agent's cached prefix + a durable distilled memory file (.egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/brc-memory.md) + the one event payload. The agent acts (review/ACK/NACK/propose/confirm), updates its memory, and exits naturally — exit code 0 is success, not a restart trigger. The wrapper loops until the orchestrator reports the role consensus-confirmed and is_complete. This removes the model-driven re-entry seam at the root of the qwen3.7-max fall-out (#2906) — the entire BRC-wait bug lineage (#2323, #2064/#2482, #2036, #1995, #2451) becomes inapplicable because the model no longer drives the wait. The agent primitive (pod, worktree, role, SDK, gateway-enforced file-write boundary, EGG_AGENT_ROLE) is untouched. The change is deletion-heavy inside the consensus subsystem: the 3-restart FAIL cap (consensus_wrapper.py:38), the `_RECOVERY_SYSTEM_PROMPT` + `_RECOVERY_USER_PROMPT` recovery machinery (consensus_wrapper.py:64-105), the SSE consensus.reached blocking path in the wrapper (consensus_wrapper.py:397-548), and the agent's `_start_wait_loop_heartbeat` ticker (sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/message.py:234-264) all go away. Per operator decisions: cq-1 splits the 28-MCP-tool collapse to a follow-up issue but requires this issue ship any net-new CLI verbs the new wrapper invokes; cq-2 ships Qwen on the new event-pump directly (no legacy fallback); cq-3 makes durable server-side persistence of the no-progress safety budget + parked HITL decision a HARD requirement (must survive SDLC-host failure); cq-4 deletes the old capped-restart wrapper path entirely with no flagged fallback.

recommended_approach.name: Stateless event-pump wrapper + durable per-role memory + server-side next-action endpoint; SDK-native `claude -p` per event; legacy capped-restart wrapper deleted in-issue
recommended_approach.summary: The wrapper is the deterministic outer loop; the agent is a per-event handler. Three new server-side primitives carry continuity (next-action endpoint, durable HITL/safety-budget persistence) and per-agent memory (.egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/brc-memory.md). The 28 agent-facing MCP tools are NOT collapsed in this issue (cq-1 follow-up) but the CLI verbs the wrapper-driven per-event handler invokes (`egg-orch brc list-blocking`, `egg-contract get-context`, the next-action verb) ARE built net-new in slice-2 so the event-pump has full CLI coverage from day one.
why_recommended: Removes the model-driven re-entry seam that this entire bug lineage depends on (the issue's root cause): `message_wait_loop` (sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/message.py:267, line :405-410 first-match return) returns on a single event, requiring the model to volunteer to re-enter the wait. Claude usually re-enters; qwen3.7-max does not (#2906) and exits success=True at ~30-50 of a 1000-turn budget. A deterministic outer loop in bash + `egg-orch message wait-loop` cannot fall out of the wait regardless of model.

Net-removes custom code: the BRC mechanism converges to the SDK-native one-shot pattern (`claude -p`) the rest of egg already uses. The bash wrapper shrinks dramatically (the 700-line `_CONSENSUS_WRAPPER_TEMPLATE` is mostly recovery + restart machinery being deleted). The 28 agent-facing MCP tools and 8 namespace files are untouched in THIS issue (cq-1 follow-up) but the action surface for the event-pump is the existing `egg-orch` / `egg-contract` CLIs, which already share handler functions with the MCP tools (sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py:2528-2805 + the shared dispatch pattern verified by tests/tools/test_mcp_cli_drift.py).

Inherits gateway-enforced file-write boundaries unchanged: each per-event `claude -p` invocation runs in the same pod with the same EGG_AGENT_ROLE env var → tool_interceptor.check_file_write_permission (shared/egg_agent/tool_interceptor.py:27) on the sandbox side, validate_agent_push on the gateway side (gateway/agent_restrictions.py, imported at gateway/phase_filter.py:1081-1083). `.egg-state/agent-outputs/` is already in every plan/refine/reviewer role's allowlist (shared/egg_restrictions/patterns.py:362,372,382,397,436-484,488), so brc-memory.md doesn't require an allowlist change.

Satisfies cq-3's durable persistence requirement: the parked HITL decision + the no-progress safety-budget state are written to the orchestrator's contract store (.egg-state/contracts/<pid>.json + branch-committed via the existing schemaVersion 1.2 migrator pattern), not held in the host process. On host death + restart, a new host re-reads the contract state and resumes from the parked decision and budget without losing either.

Per-route caching is a measured non-issue for both routes under the new control flow at the short/medium timescales (#2908 comments): the Anthropic route has a 1h TTL with the dynamic <env> sitting in the uncached suffix (no commit/cwd/date bust of the ~17K stable prefix); the Qwen route has cross-session caching (~99.99%) that survives ≥5.5min idle measured. The only remaining unknown is the Qwen TTL ceiling around 15 min worst-case BRC idle — slice-1 measures it, slice-6 conditionally adds bounded keep-warm only if that gap exists.

rejected_options_summary.B_prompt_only_mitigation_for_qwen: Tighten the BRC preamble's stay-alive language to nudge qwen3.7-max into re-entering wait_loop. Rejected because it narrows the seam for one model rather than removing it; the issue body explicitly calls this out ("prompt-only mitigations only narrow the seam for one model; they don't remove it"). Past stack-loop guard bugs (#2036, #1995, #2451, #2323, #2064, #2482) all stem from the agent-held wait assumption and would recur on the next prompt-fragile model.
rejected_options_summary.C_custom_streaming_harness_with_resume: Build a persistent streaming session with `--resume` so the agent never tears down between events. Rejected because (a) it adds a third execution structure to egg (alongside one-shot agents and the BRC consensus subsystem) — exactly the custom-harness path the issue body explicitly excludes ("no custom harness; drops the persistent-streaming-session idea entirely"); (b) the `--resume` thread retains the model-driven re-entry property that this issue is trying to delete.
rejected_options_summary.D_keep_legacy_wrapper_behind_flag: Ship the new event-pump path beside the old capped-restart wrapper, keep the old path as a flagged opt-out. Rejected by cq-4: operator explicitly directed "delete the old capped-restart wrapper path entirely — do NOT retain it behind a flag". The no-progress safety budget from cq-3 becomes the SOLE safety net under the new design.

slices.name: WS0 de-risking spike — event-pump prototype + Qwen cache TTL measurement
slices.summary: Build a minimal throwaway wrapper that loops `claude -p` per BRC event against the existing wait-loop CLI + existing MCP tool surface, run it on the #2906 reproducer (issue-2270, qwen3.7-max), and measure Qwen-route provider-cache survival across the full worst-case BRC idle (~15 min target — observed BRC idles reached 10-13 min for a producer composing a response to a NACK). Output: a `docs/spike/` report (architect / doc-updater write-scoped) covering (a) consensus reached without the 3-restart churn that motivated this issue; (b) Qwen-route TTL measured from the litellm / `cost_callback` state files (`~/.local/state/clm/cost-*.json`), since Claude Code's `usage.*` returns all-zero on the Qwen route; (c) per-event cold-read cost across consecutive per-event invocations and across the injected long idle. Anthropic-route TTL is already cleared in the WS7 empirical comment (1h, env in uncached suffix). Findings shape slice-2 next-action and slice-6 cache decisions but do not block slice-2/3/4/5 design.
slices.evidence: consensus_wrapper.py:116-713 (existing template to prototype against); sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/message.py:267 (`message_wait_loop` already provides the long-block primitive needed by the prototype); #2906 reproducer is issue-2270 on qwen3.7-max (WS0 spike scope per the issue body).

slices.name: Server-side next-action endpoint + net-new CLI verbs + durable HITL/safety-budget persistence schema
slices.summary: Land the additive primitives the production event-pump consumes, all on the orchestrator + sandbox/egg_lib side, with zero behavior change to consensus_wrapper or the agent prompt. Three pieces bundled because they share file categories: (a) `consensus next-action --role R` HTTP endpoint on the orchestrator that returns the next action the role should take — judgment stays with the agent, the endpoint owns sequencing only; extending `egg-orch consensus status --json` (sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py:2783, the existing CLI verb shared with `mcp__brc__get_state` per orch_cli.py:2785-2805) is preferred over a new verb if the existing payload is sufficient; (b) net-new CLI verbs the wrapper-driven handler invokes: `egg-orch brc list-blocking` (today only `mcp__brc__list_blocking`), `egg-contract get-context` (today only `mcp__phase__get_context`), `egg-orch brc next-action` if (a) takes the new-verb path, plus `egg-orch consensus check` idempotent recovery helpers if needed — all via `_handler_dispatch` so they share existing MCP handlers (preserves tests/tools/test_mcp_cli_drift.py invariant); (c) durable persistence schema for `pipeline.no_progress_budget` + the parked-HITL state needed to survive SDLC-host failure (cq-3 HARD requirement), landed on `.egg-state/contracts/<pid>.json` via the existing schemaVersion migrator pattern. No consumers wired yet — purely additive schema and CLI surface.
slices.evidence: sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py:2528 (consensus propose), :2633 (ack), :2692 (nack), :2753 (confirmed), :2783 (status); sandbox/egg_lib/contract_cli.py:342 (show), :737 (add-decision), 1249 (add-feedback) — confirming no `phase get-context` CLI verb today; tests/tools/test_mcp_cli_drift.py (CLI parity gate to extend); orchestrator/contract_store.py:136 (`.egg-state/contracts/<pid>.json` is authoritative + branch-committed, providing the durable persistence backstop cq-3 requires); orchestrator/contract_store.py:127-167 (`load_contract_from_branch` reads from origin/<branch> then local — the recovery path on host death).

slices.name: `brc-memory.md` artifact + brc_ack/brc_nack handler memory-write scaffolding
slices.summary: Define the durable per-role memory file that carries continuity between per-event `claude -p` invocations, and wire its writes into the handler layer that already runs on every ACK/NACK. The file format is markdown with structured sections (codebase/change model, per-producer assessment, decision log) anchored by stable headings so the agent can read-modify-write deterministically. Written to `.egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/brc-memory.md`. brc_ack and brc_nack already receive `reason` + `files_reviewed` from the agent (sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/brc.py — existing brc handler module), so the handler appends a structured entry to the memory file on each ACK/NACK rather than leaving curation to the model. Retention treatment per refine Q2: ephemeral coordination state cleaned up with the pod; the orchestrator message history is the durable reconstruction backstop. The hard caveat from refine Q2 stands: if implement-time evidence shows the memory file is load-bearing for correct recovery after host/pod restart, this slice is revisited and the artifact made durable. Memory shape (append-only vs rewrite-and-distill — open decision #1 in the issue body) is decided here against the slice-1 spike's measured Qwen TTL: if the cache survives long enough for delta analysis to dominate prefix-cache cost, choose rewrite-and-distill (bounded growth); otherwise append-only with tail compaction.
slices.evidence: shared/egg_restrictions/patterns.py:362-484 (`.egg-state/agent-outputs/` is in every plan/refine/reviewer role's allowlist — no allowlist tweak needed for `<role>/` subdirs); sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/brc.py (existing brc_ack/brc_nack handlers receive reason + files_reviewed); .egg-state/agent-outputs/ today is flat (e.g. 2769-architect-output.json, issue-2777-replan-architect-output.json) — this slice introduces the per-role subdir convention; refine feedback Q2 resolution (ephemeral cleanup-with-pod, host-recovery from message history).

slices.name: Event-pump consensus_wrapper + wrapper-side liveness migration + safety-budget consumer + legacy deletion
slices.summary: The central control-flow rewrite. The wrapper becomes a deterministic event pump: blocks on `egg-orch message wait-loop`, invokes `claude -p` per actionable event, and loops until the orchestrator reports the role consensus-confirmed and is_complete. Four tightly-coupled pieces: (a) WS1 — rewrite `_CONSENSUS_WRAPPER_TEMPLATE` (orchestrator/consensus_wrapper.py:116-713); clean agent exit after handling one event is expected, not a restart trigger; delete `MAX_CONSENSUS_RESTARTS = 3` (consensus_wrapper.py:38), the restart loop (consensus_wrapper.py:555-695), `_RECOVERY_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (consensus_wrapper.py:64-99), `_RECOVERY_USER_PROMPT` (consensus_wrapper.py:102-105), and the SSE consensus.reached blocking path (consensus_wrapper.py:397-548) — cq-4 mandates no flagged fallback at any point; (b) WS4 — move heartbeat + gateway-session keep-alive ownership from the agent's `_start_wait_loop_heartbeat` ticker (sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/message.py:175 + lines 234-264, fires every `_WAIT_LOOP_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECS = 60s` at message.py:47) to the wrapper's wait, because the agent's wait_loop no longer holds the long wait; the orchestrator-side heartbeat threshold consumer (orchestrator/health_monitor.py:771, 120s default / 600s implement) is unchanged; (c) safety-budget consumer wired against the durable `pipeline.no_progress_budget` field from slice-2 — when exhausted, fire OVERSEER_ALERT + open a HITL decision (resume/abort) using the durable parked-HITL state from slice-2; on host death + restart, the wrapper re-reads the durable state and resumes monitoring the same budget (cq-3 HARD requirement); (d) the SSE blocking path collapses to a single `egg-orch consensus check` against the slice-2 endpoint — orchestrator/sse.py:111 (SSEClientManager) stays for the operator-facing stream (out of scope per cq-1); orchestrator/concurrent_executor.py:37 import of `build_consensus_wrapped_command` is rewired to the new template. Minimal agent-prompt change: drop the stay-alive loop instruction from `_build_brc_preamble` (orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:12348, called at :13659, :13692, :13720) — the FULL preamble collapse stays in slice-5.

slices.name: Prompt collapse + delta-scoped re-analysis
slices.summary: Retire the agent-side mechanics the agent no longer owns now that the wrapper drives the loop. Two coupled pieces (both touch agent prompts and the per-event context payload): (a) WS6 prompt collapse — replace the STAY-ALIVE / wait-loop / cursor-threading / pre-confirm-wait foot-gun text in `_build_brc_preamble` (orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:12348) and in sandbox/agent-config/rules/*.md (the existing rule files: mission.md, overseer.md, etc.) with a lean event-handler contract: "here is the one event; handle it; exit cleanly; the wrapper handles the rest" plus the few invariants the agent still owns (file-write boundary, prose via stdin/file for propose/ack/nack); also remove the now-redundant `egg-orch message wait-loop` examples from the preamble since the agent no longer calls it; (b) WS5 delta-scoped re-analysis — extend the slice-2 next-action endpoint to additionally return `changed_artifacts` + version delta + the agent's prior memory file pointer, and update the per-event prompt template to say "evaluate ONLY the named changed_artifacts against the prior memory; do not re-read the codebase / earlier commits / the analysis draft" — bounds per-event context to a delta. The handler-side adapter that fetches the delta lives in sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/brc.py and is wired via the slice-2 net-new CLI verb. No wrapper changes here.
slices.evidence: orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:12348 (_build_brc_preamble); sandbox/agent-config/rules/mission.md (overall agent rules file); docs/reference/agent-wait-patterns.md (existing wait-loop pattern docs to retire/rewrite); the next-action endpoint contract is established in slice-2.

slices.name: Qwen-route bounded keep-warm cache refinement (conditional on slice-1 spike data)
slices.summary: Decide whether bounded keep-warm is needed on the Qwen route based on the slice-1 spike's measured TTL ceiling, and ship only if needed. Three outcomes possible: (a) slice-1 data shows the Qwen provider cache survives the full worst-case BRC idle (≥ ~15 min observed worst case) — slice-6 collapses to a docs note in docs/architecture/brc-event-pump.md ("no keep-warm needed on either route, confirmed by slice-1 measurement"), no production code; (b) slice-1 data shows the Qwen cache lapses between 5.5 and ~15 min — slice-6 adds a bounded keep-warm to the wrapper (NOT the agent) that fires only on the Qwen route, only during reviewer-parked-on-NACK idles where the wait is approaching the measured TTL, with a hard cap on total refreshes and an explicit suppression while in HITL / awaiting-human waits (which can last hours and would burn Qwen tokens against an event hours away); (c) slice-1 data is ambiguous — slice-6 opens a HITL decision asking the operator to choose. Anthropic route is out of scope (1h TTL already cleared in the WS7 empirical comment).
slices.evidence: #2908 issue body WS7 (route-specific scope: Anthropic measured-clear, Qwen TTL ceiling open); cq-2 resolution ("WS0 must instrument the actual per-event cold-read / cache-creation cost on the Qwen route across a realistic worst-case BRC idle ... ONLY if that measured cold-read waste proves material should a BOUNDED keep-warm be added, and then: Qwen-route only ... SUPPRESSED during HITL / awaiting-human waits").

constraints: cq-1 (resolved): The 28-MCP-tool collapse goes to a FOLLOW-UP issue. This issue MUST build any net-new CLI verbs the new wait-loop / event-pump depends on (`brc get-state`, `brc list-blocking`, `phase get-context`, plus any other tool the per-event handler invokes). Do NOT delete existing MCP tools in this issue.

cq-2 (resolved): Ship Qwen route ENABLED on the new event-pump (no fallback to the old path — that path is being deleted per cq-4). Both routes confirmed to have a free cache TTL > 5 minutes. WS0 must instrument per-event cold-read cost across a realistic worst-case BRC idle (~7-8 min in practice). ONLY if measured cold-read waste proves material should a BOUNDED keep-warm be added — Qwen-route only, active only during idles approaching the TTL, with a capped total number of refreshes, and SUPPRESSED during HITL / awaiting-human waits.

cq-3 (resolved): When the no-progress safety budget is exhausted, fire OVERSEER_ALERT + open a HITL decision (resume/abort). HARD REQUIREMENT: the parked HITL decision AND the safety-budget / no-progress state MUST be persisted DURABLY SERVER-SIDE in the orchestrator, not held only in the host process. If the host running the SDLC pipeline dies, a restarted host must be able to resume the awaiting-human decision and the budget state.

cq-4 (resolved): Delete the old capped-restart wrapper path ENTIRELY in this issue. NO flagged fallback at any point. The event-pump replaces it outright. The no-progress safety budget from cq-3 is the sole safety net.

Refine feedback Q1 (resolved): WS0 measures and reports per-pipeline token spend, per-event wall-clock, and (if ever built) keep-warm-loop $/hour; nothing auto-fails on a fixed threshold; operator judges go/no-go from reported numbers.

Refine feedback Q2 (resolved): `brc-memory.md` is treated as EPHEMERAL coordination state (cleaned up with the pod); orchestrator message history is the durable reconstruction backstop. HARD CAVEAT: if implement-time evidence shows the memory file is load-bearing for correct recovery after host/pod restart, this is revisited.

WS8 hard constraint (from issue body): prose-bearing commands (`consensus propose/ack/nack` — `reason`, `files_reviewed`) must take text via stdin OR a file path, NEVER argv — argv routes prose through Bash's `bash -c`, reintroducing the shell-metachar corruption mitigated in #2741. Slice-2 net-new CLI verbs must enforce this.
File-write boundary preserved: every per-event `claude -p` invocation runs in the same pod with the same EGG_AGENT_ROLE env var; sandbox interceptor + gateway push validator unchanged.
`.egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/` writes need NO allowlist tweak — shared/egg_restrictions/patterns.py:362-484 already covers the prefix for every plan/refine/reviewer role.
Agent primitive untouched: pod shape, worktree per role, EGG_AGENT_ROLE plumbing, SDK invocation, MCP tool registration — all preserved by this issue.
concurrent_executor.py:95 ConcurrentPhaseExecutor's role-spawn shape unchanged — the wrapper command inside the pod changes, the pod itself does not.
Health monitor (orchestrator/health_monitor.py:771) thresholds unchanged (120s default / 600s implement) — wrapper-side heartbeat in slice-4 fires at the same rate.

risks_for_risk_analyst.name: Single-slice rewrite of consensus_wrapper.py is large (700+ lines, near-complete rewrite)
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Slice-4 scope is intentionally tight (wrapper template + minimal prompt edit + deletion of three closely-tied code blocks). cq-4 forbids splitting via flagged fallback. If the BRC cycle hits >3 NACK rounds, task_planner should subdivide along the orchestrator-side vs sandbox-side seam (already an option called out in the slice scaffold).

risks_for_risk_analyst.name: Safety budget exhausted on host restart before durable state writes
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: cq-3 explicitly requires durable server-side persistence + recovery on host death. Slice-2 schema lands first; slice-4 wrapper only writes after slice-2 ships. Integration test in slice-4 must inject a synthetic host-kill mid-budget and verify a fresh host resumes from the persisted state.

risks_for_risk_analyst.name: memory file becomes load-bearing for recovery despite refine Q2 ephemeral treatment
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Refine Q2 hard caveat invokes: if implement-time evidence shows the memory file is load-bearing, slice-3 is revisited and the artifact is made durable. Slice-4 integration test must explicitly inject a memory-file-loss scenario and verify the agent reconstructs from the orchestrator message history without observable failure.

risks_for_risk_analyst.name: Qwen route TTL ceiling lands in the 5.5-15min gap, requiring keep-warm
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Slice-6 explicitly handles three outcomes including bounded keep-warm with cost caps and HITL/awaiting-human suppression. Operator-confirmed Qwen token costs are low so worst-case cold-read waste is bounded.

risks_for_risk_analyst.name: Prompt collapse in slice-5 strands behavior the wrapper assumes
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Slice-4 makes the MINIMAL prompt edit (drop stay-alive only); slice-5 makes the cleanup pass. If slice-4 lands and slice-5 NACKs on prompt-vs-wrapper drift, the contract is: revert slice-5 only, slice-4 keeps shipping. Prompt and wrapper changes are independently revertable.

risks_for_risk_analyst.name: MCP tools left in place by cq-1 conflict with per-event handler
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: MCP tools and CLI verbs share handlers (`_handler_dispatch` pattern verified by tests/tools/test_mcp_cli_drift.py). The wrapper-driven handler uses CLI; the model inside `claude -p` may still call MCP tools — same handlers run in both cases. cq-1 follow-up issue collapses the duplication.

risks_for_risk_analyst.name: Cursor-threading regression (#2323) when wrapper drives wait-loop cadence
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Existing `/tmp/egg-wait-cursor-${EGG_PIPELINE_ID}-${EGG_AGENT_ROLE}-*` mechanism is process-local; the wrapper invokes wait-loop in the same pod where the agent ran before, so the cursor file path is the same. Slice-4 unit + integration tests must explicitly cover a send→wait race across a per-event boundary.

risks_for_risk_analyst.name: Per-event cold-read cost on Qwen route exceeds operator-acceptable per-cycle budget
risks_for_risk_analyst.mitigation: Slice-1 spike measures per-event cold-read cost; refine Q1 explicitly directed instrumentation-only (no auto-fail thresholds). Operator judges go/no-go from reported numbers.
